quick.topic: Know the decision before the slides
quick.summary: Why slides wander, and the one sentence to write before you open them.
quick.takeaway: Name the decision first. Every slide helps them make it.

parts.title: Know the decision before the slides

beats.line: Two days on slides. Why did my manager ask what I wanted?
Did you know what you wanted before slide one?
Roughly. I hoped it would come out.
Start from the decision you want the room to make.
Write it as one question they can answer yes or no.

board.text: the decision, as a yes or no

beats.line: Then plan only the slides they need to answer it.

board.text: only what they need to answer

beats.line: What if I don’t know what they’ll decide?
You don’t need their answer. Just the question you are asking.
End on that same question, so they decide in the room.
We should fund the mobile fix this quarter. Yes or no?
Now every slide has somewhere to go.

quiz.question: What should you write before building any slides?
options: The decision you want the room to make
quiz.explanation: Knowing the decision tells you which slides help and which to cut.

quiz.question: You need to know what the audience will decide before you build your slides.
quiz.explanation: You need the decision you are asking them for, not their answer.
